pub_title: Profiling people with Parkinson's disease at risk of cognitive decline: Insights from PPMI and ICICLE‐PD data
dataset_context_from_paper: Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI) data were used, accessed on November 15, 2022. PPMI is an international, observational, cohort study with almost 50 sites across 13 countries. Eligibility was contingent on a diagnosis of PD no longer than 2 years prior to enrolment and drug naïve status. Participants with young-onset PD (age < 50) and dementia were excluded. Data were available annually from baseline up to year 7. Participants with two or more data points were included, resulting in N= 770 baseline participants. Latent class mixed models were created to identify subgroups with similar longitudinal cognitive trajectories using total MoCA score as the outcome variable.
dataset_keywords: Parkinson's disease, cognitive decline, longitudinal cohort

pub_title: Profiling people with Parkinson's disease at risk of cognitive decline: Insights from PPMI and ICICLE‐PD data
dataset_context_from_paper: Incidence of Cognitive Impairment in Cohorts with Longitudinal Evaluation-Parkinson's Disease (ICICLE-PD) data were used, accessed on October 10, 2022. ICICLE-PD was conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki and GCP guidelines. Ethical approval was provided by the Newcastle and North Tyneside Research Ethics Committee. Recruitment took place from the community in Cambridgeshire and Newcastle upon Tyne/Gateshead, United Kingdom. All participants were recently diagnosed people with PD meeting Queen's Square Brain Bank Criteria, with working knowledge of English and no significant baseline cognitive impairment. Data were available every 18-months from baseline to year 4.5. Participants with two or more data points were included, resulting in N= 212 baseline participants. Latent class mixed models were applied to identify cognitive subtypes based on rate of decline in MoCA scores.
dataset_keywords: Parkinson's disease, cognitive impairment, community-based cohort

pub_title: Early-stage idiopathic Parkinson’s disease is associated with reduced circular RNA expression
dataset_context_from_paper: The Michael J Fox Foundation Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI) cohort was used as the discovery cohort. dataset_keywords: Parkinson's disease, whole blood RNA sequencing, early-stage idiopathic PD

Funded by the National Institute on Aging, LEADS seeks to define EOAD and its variants, to understand its progression, to find clinical outcome measures and surrogate biomarkers that can be of use in clinical trials for EOAD, to understand the impact of EOAD on people living with dementia and families, and to find resources to assist them. LEADS was designed to enroll and follow 500 people with EOAD from >15 sites in the United States. Approximately 75% of people enrolled in LEADS with early-onset cognitive impairment or dementia have evidence of elevated brain amyloid, which confirms the AD diagnosis; the remaining 25% are negative for amyloid. The distribution of tau in the brain differs between EOAD and late-onset AD, and also varies between the different EOAD types.
dataset_keywords: early-onset Alzheimer's disease, biomarkers, longitudinal study

Participants were fluent in English, had a knowledgeable informant, without pathogenic variants in APP, PSEN1, PSEN2, GRN, or MAPT or repeat expansions in C9ORF72, and had CDR global score ≤1 at enrollment.

pub_title: LD-informed deep learning for Alzheimer’s gene loci detection using WGS data

The ADSP participants have WGS data sequenced using multiple platforms, including IlluminaHiSeq2000 and IlluminaHiSeqXTen. This release (R3) includes 16,906 whole-genome sequences (WGS), processed and curated as part of the project. The release contains CRAMs, gVCFs, and quality-controlled project-level VCFs (pVCFs) for autosomal biallelic single nucleotide variants (SNVs) and indels, along with structural variant (SV) calls generated by Manta, Smoove, and Strelka variant callers. dataset_context_from_paper: The DeFi trial was an international, double-blind, randomized placebo-controlled trial using nirogacestat 150 mg twice a day. PFS was the primary endpoint, with progression event consisting of clinical progression, radiological progression (using MRI scans) or death. At a median follow-up of 15.9 months, the median PFS was not reached with nirogacestat as opposed to 15.1 months in the placebo group. dataset_context_from_paper: In January 2021, the SCAN initiative was implemented to standardize imaging acquisition protocols and analysis pipelines for PET and MRI, mirroring image standardization in ADNI. SCAN includes ADRC imaging data acquired after January 2021 that follow the standardized SCAN pre-processing protocol. Authors implemented an identical post-processing MRI-free pipeline that is currently applied to SCAN PET data to make MP PET data as comparable as possible to SCAN.
dataset_keywords: ['standardized PET imaging', 'MRI neuroimaging', "Alzheimer's disease research"]

dataset_context_from_paper: As a comparison to another standardized PET dataset, authors examined amyloid PET data from ADNI, given that nearly identical standardization workflows have been implemented in ADNI and SCAN. ADNI is a multi-site longitudinal study designed to validate biomarkers for use in AD clinical trials. All data generated by the ADNI study are available via LONI for download. Step 4 summed PET images with a series description of '* Coreg, Avg, Std Img and Vox Siz, Uniform *Res*' were downloaded from LONI on May 21, 2024 and processed.
dataset_keywords: ['amyloid PET', 'biomarker validation', 'multi-site longitudinal study']

dataset_context_from_paper: The datasets generated and/or analysed during the current study are available in the Zenodo repository. The study includes biomarker and genetic data from Parkinson's disease patients, including cerebrospinal fluid seed amplification assay (SAA) results and genetic variants (GBA, LRRK2, PRKN, SNCA). Data stratified by device-aided therapy (DAT) status and deep brain stimulation (DBS) treatment, with clinical characteristics including cognitive assessment (MoCA) and motor symptoms (PIGD).
dataset_keywords: ["Parkinson's disease", 'genetic variants', 'biomarkers']

dataset_context_from_paper: Data from National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center (NACC) containing n = 49,412 cases. Authors applied selection criteria excluding cases with specific medical history (stroke, Parkinson's disease, alcohol abuse, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, depression within two years, traumatic brain injury, or other neurological disease) at baseline or with dominantly-inherited AD mutations. Further restricted to cases with Clinical Dementia Rating global score (CDR-GS) of 0 at baseline and available APOE genotype data (n = 11,668). Final analysis included n = 9,306 unique cases aged 40 or older with multiple study site visits. Event of interest was first development of dementia defined as CDR-GS ≥ 1 during observation period. Dataset includes Clinical Dementia Rating Global Score, Clinical Dementia Rating Sum of Boxes, Mini-Mental State Examination scores, positron emission tomography data, cerebrospinal fluid measurements, and amyloid data (obtained in subset of participants).
dataset_keywords: ["Alzheimer's disease", 'dementia progression', 'APOE genotype']

dataset_context_from_paper: The present work investigated relationships between depressive symptoms and cognition in the Kuakini-HAAS cohort at baseline and over 20 years of follow-up. Depressive symptoms in conjunction with APOE ε4 were associated with greater dementia risk in the Kuakini Honolulu-Asia Aging Study (HAAS). The study examined three CES-D subscales (depressed affect, somatic complaints, and positive affect) as predictors of change in global cognitive performance. A two-factor CASI model representing crystallized (cognitive domains of long-term memory, orientation, visual construction, judgment, and language abilities) and fluid (short-term memory, attention, mental manipulation, and list-generating fluency) dimensions has provided a good fit to the Kuakini-HAAS CASI data. APOE and FOXO3 genotypes were included as covariates in multivariable regression analyses. Each analysis was conducted for all study participants who had complete data at each visit (longitudinal sample) and the subset of participants who had valid data at all timepoints (termed 'Exam 12 survivors').
dataset_keywords: ['cognitive aging', 'depressive symptoms', 'genetic variants']

data_repository: Not publicly available - available on request

All models were fitted in the same sample of individuals with subjective cognitive decline (SCD) from BioFINDER-1 and BioFINDER-2 cohorts (n = 469), after multiple imputation of missing data. The study included APOE4 genotype data, biomarker measurements, and demographic variables.

dataset_context_from_paper: Single-cell RNA sequencing data have been archived in the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) under accession number GEO: GSE308594. The Seurat function 'FindMarkers' was employed to perform differential expression analysis and identify variations among different samples within the clusters. Parameters of |log2fold change| > 0.25 and p-value-adj <0.05 were established as thresholds for identifying differentially expressed genes (DEGs). Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses were conducted using the clusterProfiler package (v4.10.0) in conjunction with the org.Mm.eg.db database (v3.18.0), retaining only enriched terms with p-values less than 0.05.

The data will be available for open access upon publication. Bioinformatics analyses were carried out utilising R (version 4.2.0) along with associated Bioconductor packages. Selection criteria for significant findings were based on an adjusted p-value using the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) method for multiple testing correction, with a threshold of less than 0.05, coupled with an absolute log2 Fold Change exceeding 0.3785. Functional enrichment analysis was conducted using the clusterProfiler package for Gene Ontology and KEGG enrichment analyses.

dataset_context_from_paper: Cross sectional data from the National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center's Uniform Data Set was analyzed to examine the association between functional hearing loss and neuropsychiatric symptoms (NPS) in persons living with dementia. The study included 10,054 participants with a mean age of 75 (SD 8) years. Of these, 2,416 (24%) self-reported functional hearing loss with 3.4 (SD 2.5) mean total number of NPS and mean NPS severity of 5.1 (SD 4.9). Negative binomial regression with robust variance was used to estimate associations adjusting for demographic and clinical characteristics. In the subsample with hearing loss (n=1,325, 54.8%), nearest neighbor matching based on respondent demographic characteristics was used to address selection bias for hearing aid use.
dataset_keywords: ['dementia', 'neuropsychiatric symptoms', 'hearing loss']

dataset_context_from_paper: The raw datasets analyzed during the current study are publicly available from the Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI) database. PASE was added to PPMI de novo cohort after the start of the trial. The earliest available value for each participant was used. PPMI has a relatively high retention rate; however, retention biases that have the potential to impact cognitive outcomes are still likely to be present. In this study, there were more participants who completed the study (n = 355; 84.9%) than participants who did not (n = 63; 15.1%). The SD for CCS at baseline and final study visit across these groups were very similar.

Data from electronic medical records (EMR) were extracted automatically. Preexisting comorbidities included body mass index (BMI), congestive heart failure (CHF), chronic kidney disease (CKD), hypertension, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and asthma that were designated by ICD10 codes at admission or prior. Hospitalization status and intensive-care-unit (ICU) admission were also extracted.

dataset_context_from_paper: Phase 1 established tiered criteria by evaluating 23 nominated loci across study designs. Phase 2 applied this framework to 29 large-scale genome-wide studies published since 2015, tiering 163 unique loci. Phase 1 yielded 17 high-confidence loci (12 linked to specific genes), and Phase 2 identified 111 high-confidence loci/genes with replicated associations across ancestries and convergent single-variant/variant-set evidence. Prioritized loci highlight APP processing, microglial immunity, and lipid metabolism pathways, including genes not captured by existing resources like Agora or Open Targets. Summarized results can be viewed at https://topgenes.niagads.org/.

PPMI is a public-private partnership funded by the Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson's Research. The study used PPMI data to develop disease-duration-specific subtyping algorithms for Parkinson's disease, with analysis of selective dropout from PPMI by baseline data-driven subtype.

dataset_context_from_paper: CSF DDC measurements are available in the PPMI database (project 274). All samples from the PPMI cohort were run on the same day on four plates with four quality control samples (CSF pools) on each plate. The newly developed SMC assay was used to quantify DDC levels in cerebrospinal fluid samples from drug-naïve Parkinson's disease patients and controls, achieving an AUC of 0.89 in ROC analysis for discriminating dopaminergic drug-naïve PD patients from controls.
dataset_keywords: ['cerebrospinal fluid', 'DDC protein biomarker', "Parkinson's disease"]

dataset_context_from_paper: The cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarker data used in this study were obtained from the Accelerating Medicines Partnership-Parkinson's disease (AMP-PD) consortium under approved data access agreements. AMP-PD cohort with PD, control, and SWEDD participants and six CSF biomarkers (Aβ42, α-syn, t-tau, p-tau181, hemoglobin). Preprocessing included missing-value imputation, standardization, and outlier screening. Five machine-learning models were trained with stratified 5-fold cross-validation. Data balancing used the SMOTE-Tomek method with performance evaluation based on AUC, PR-AUC, and Brier score.

The interface accepts numeric CSF biomarker values within physiologically plausible ranges (Aβ42, α-syn, t-tau, p-tau181, hemoglobin) and applies the same preprocessing pipeline used during model training.

ADNI participant data were analyzed in this study. Data collection and sharing for the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) is funded by the National Institute on Aging (National Institutes of Health Grant U19 AG024904).

dataset_context_from_paper: MIMIC-III, an EHR dataset focusing on intensive care settings, used to assess the effectiveness of the proposed VTDNet framework. The study leveraged real-world electronic health record (EHR) data to estimate individualized treatment effects (ITE) in longitudinal observational settings. VTDNet achieved lower root mean squared error, mean absolute error, and influence function precision in the estimation of heterogeneous effects compared to existing state-of-the-art methods on this real-world EHR dataset.

Used as a real-world dataset to assess the effectiveness of the proposed VTDNet framework for estimating individualized treatment effects in longitudinal settings. VTDNet achieves lower root mean squared error, mean absolute error, and influence function precision in the estimation of heterogeneous effects compared to existing state-of-the-art methods on this real-world EHR dataset.

Experimental results on the synthetic dataset demonstrate superior accuracy under varying levels of confounding, validating the framework's ability to handle hidden confounding in controlled conditions.

dataset_context_from_paper: This study is a secondary analysis of de-identified data obtained from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI). ADNI data are available from the LONI Image and Data Archive subject to the ADNI Data Use Agreement. The dataset was used to develop and validate predictive models for cognitive decline, specifically examining the relationship between domain-specific cognitive measures and CDR-SB (Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes) scores. Participants were eligible with ≥3 item-level visits. The analysis demonstrated R² values of 0.497 for the inferred mask and 0.674 for total score in predicting CDR-SB.

This study is a secondary analysis of de-identified data from the National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center (NACC). The dataset was used alongside ADNI for validation of predictive models for cognitive decline. In NACC, the 19-item saturated vector substantially exceeded the total score (R² 0.707 vs 0.593) in predicting CDR-SB, showing that item-level detail carries clinically relevant information. Participants were eligible with ≥3 item-level visits.
dataset_keywords: ["Alzheimer's disease", 'cognitive assessment', 'longitudinal observational']

Participants in each study were administered the FCI-SF, which evaluates coin/currency calculation, financial conceptual knowledge, use of a checkbook/register, and use of a bank statement.

Participants in each study were administered the FCI-SF, which evaluates coin/currency calculation, financial conceptual knowledge, use of a checkbook/register, and use of a bank statement.

Participants (n = 202, mean age of 78 years, 38% female) with diagnoses of cognitive unimpairment (n = 109), mild cognitive impairment (n = 71), and dementia (n = 22) were included. p-Tau217 was determined using the ALZpath Simoa p-tau217 immunoassay and an immunoprecipitation mass spectrometry assay. Amyloid positivity was defined by amyloid-PET with a centiloid of ≥25. The study investigated the relationship of plasma p-tau217 concentrations versus estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) in individuals with CKD with and without amyloid pathology.
dataset_keywords: ['plasma biomarkers', 'cognitive status', 'amyloid pathology']

Participants (n = 202, mean age of 78 years, 38% female) with diagnoses of cognitive unimpairment (n = 109), mild cognitive impairment (n = 71), and dementia (n = 22) were included. In all, 114 (56%) of all participants were amyloid-PET positive (A+) and 86 (43%) were classified as having CKD (stages 3–4). p-Tau217 concentrations were measured and analyzed in relation to eGFR and amyloid status.
dataset_keywords: ['cognitive impairment', 'chronic kidney disease', 'tau biomarkers']

The study evaluates multiple biomarker modalities including brain imaging (18-F-Florbetapir PET), cognitive assessments (PACC, MMSE, logical memory), and retinal amyloid imaging. The research examines how combinations of biomarker tests can enhance diagnostic accuracy and specificity for Alzheimer's disease, testing additional diagnostic assays across different modalities to provide insights into AD progression.

The study collects biomarker data including apolipoprotein E (APOE) genotyping and other neurodegeneration assessments to track disease progression and risk factors.

dataset_context_from_paper: Summary statistics from the GWAS in this study are available at GWAS Catalog (GCST90727422). The GWAS identified four genome-wide significant loci associated with ADAD risk, with sentinel variants on chromosomes 14 (rs141931440 near RHOJ gene, p<0.0001, OR 5.96), 1 (rs74546314 in CNIH4, p<0.0001, OR 11.99), 5 (rs537168961 near CCNG1 gene, p<0.0001, OR 9.56), and 2 (rs78120946 in ALK gene, p<0.0001, OR 7.21). Analysis included common and low-frequency variants (MAF≥0.005) using logistic Firth regression adjusted for sex, cohort, and principal components.

In this meta-analysis, RHOJ (p<0.0001, OR 5.11) and CNIH4 (p<0.0001, OR 10.16) sentinel variants reached genome-wide significance, and the CCNG1 sentinel variant was nearly genome-wide significant (p<0.0001, OR 7.47). The sentinel variants were not associated with sporadic Alzheimer's disease.

dataset_context_from_paper: The similarity between allele frequencies observed in the Genome Aggregation Database (gnomAD) database and those in control groups offers supportive evidence for the reliability and validity of the GWAS findings.
dataset_keywords: ['allele frequencies', 'population genetics', 'variant validation']

Whole genome sequencing data were classified into genotype status groups based on availability of genomic data: those with both WGS and SNP data (G2), those with SNP data only (G1), and those with no genotype data (G0). All individuals with WGS also had SNP data, providing duplicate SNV genotypes for the SNP genotypes. The use of genotype status groups allowed evaluation of, and eventual adjustment for, genotyping accuracy/error.

Each of the HISP and NHW family data sets were classified into three genotype status groups based on the availability of genomic data. The study focused on the larger HISP subset, with comparable results for NHW provided in the Supporting Information.

The dataset includes neuroimaging data from patients with frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD), including behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD), primary progressive aphasias (PPA), progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), and corticobasal syndrome (CBS). The data was used to analyze heterogeneity within and between FTLD subtypes and their neuroanatomical signatures across disease progression.
dataset_keywords: ['neuroimaging', 'frontotemporal dementia', 'disease progression']

The data was used to examine heterogeneity in FTLD subtypes and support the development of subtype-specific biomarkers and personalized diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

Genotype data from the PPMI cohort were extracted directly from whole-genome sequencing data. The SNPs of the clinically recruited participants were genotyped using the polymerase chain reaction-restriction fragment length polymorphism (PCR–RFLP) method. The dataset was used to analyze associations of AXIN1 polymorphisms (rs13337493 and rs9921222) with clinical manifestations and biomarkers in white populations with Parkinson's disease, including DATSCAN imaging, motor function assessments (H&Y stage, UPDRS), nonmotor function measures (MoCA, RBD, ESS, olfactory disorders, depression), and cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers (α-Synuclein, dopamine metabolites, tau, and amyloid-beta).

Authors used Siemens pASL sequence data (n = 123) and pCASL sequence data (n = 70) to measure cerebral blood flow (CBF). The analysis focused on cognitive status effects using relative CBF (rCBF) measurements, with data collected across multiple ADNI sites. The dataset was used with random forest machine learning methods to screen variables for predictive models of chronic diseases in relation to cognitive outcomes. MMSE covariate scores were included in models to provide adjusted estimation of effects of target chronic diseases. The dataset includes medication information covering antihypertensive therapies, lipid-lowering medications, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory medications, anticoagulant or antiplatelet agents, antidepressants, antipsychotics, anxiolytics, sedative or hypnotic agents, FDA-approved medications for Alzheimer's disease, anti-Parkinson agents, hormone therapies, and diabetes medications. Models included APOE ε4 genotype status as a variable.

The study assessed whether brain age gap (BAG) serves as a marker of disease progression by comparing BAG between Parkinson's disease (PD) progression subtypes. The research used PPMI clinical data to develop and validate BAG-based prognostic enrichment strategies that could lower the required sample size in randomized controlled trials (RCTs) by 23-58%.

dataset_context_from_paper: This study included participants with normal cognition (CN) and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative. Cognitive IIV was computed as the within-person standard deviation of five domain-specific neuropsychological test z-scores. Four neuroimaging biomarker IIV metrics were similarly derived using regional amyloid-β (n = 1,021), tau (n = 719), cortical thickness (n = 2,148), and combined amyloid-tau-neurodegeneration (ATN, n = 258). Associations between cognitive IIV and each biomarker IIV were evaluated using linear regression models, adjusted for relevant covariates.

The registry collects longitudinal cognitive and health data from volunteers to support research on neurodegenerative diseases and aging.

The comprehensive testing battery available on the DCH app includes tasks of executive functioning and memory, survey deployment infrastructure, and passive data capture via smartphone sensors, and is relevant to assessing cognition across a range of neurodegenerative and neurological conditions.

PRSs with dosage were calculated in plink, using the imputed genotypes of the PD-risk loci reported by Nalls et al. dataset_context_from_paper: This study leverages the extraordinarily rich data resources of the National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center (NACC) dataset, representing a well-characterized and multicenter sample of people living with AD. The dataset is uniquely suited for this analysis due to its breadth, rigorous diagnostic procedures, standardized collection by trained clinicians, and its large representation of EOAD—a population often underrepresented in large-scale studies. Item parameters were applied to the longitudinal data set (e.g. all visits, not just the most recent visit) to obtain factor scores for the language domain. The study leveraged a uniquely robust sample of individuals with EOAD and LOAD from a large, multi-site cohort of incident and prevalent AD from NACC. The standardized data collection across Alzheimer's Disease Research Centers (ADRCs), conducted by highly trained clinicians and research personnel with deep expertise in dementia diagnosis and assessment, ensures the clinical rigor of EOAD and LOAD classification, and ascertainment of language performance in standardized fashion across all participant encounters. Classification resulted in a participant sample of 1,189 EOAD and 4,646 LOAD.

The original goal of ADNI was to test whether serial magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), positron emission tomography (PET), other biological markers, and clinical and neuropsychological assessment can be combined to measure the progression of mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and early Alzheimer's disease (AD). The analysis was limited to structural MRI data for validating the cognitiveTree automated pipeline for dementia classification, achieving high discrimination performance (AUC = 0.90) compared to radiologists (AUC = 0.71 and 0.62).

dataset_context_from_paper: The Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) database includes longitudinal clinical, cognitive, imaging, genetic, autopsy, and biomarker data from more than 2400 participants. The resource comprises over 185,000 imaging datasets. More than 26,000 investigators across 169 countries have accessed ADNI's database, which has supported more than 405 million data downloads. Over 7000 publications have used ADNI data and/or samples. This review synthesizes 122 high-impact studies using ADNI data or biospecimens from 2023 to mid-2025 to clarify mechanisms of Alzheimer's disease progression. By integrating imaging, fluid biomarkers, genetics, and clinical measures, ADNI provides a comprehensive research dataset for unraveling mechanisms underlying AD progression.

dataset_context_from_paper: Data are drawn from the National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center Uniform Data Set (NACCUDS). Data from the ADRCs are anonymized and compiled into the NACCUDS, widely recognized as the gold standard in longitudinal, multi-domain neurocognitive and phenotypic data. Data used in the current study were drawn from all participants age 50 or older who were enrolled in NACCUDS until the November 2022 data freeze and had at least one follow-up visit. Participants diagnosed as MCI or AD at baseline with a primary etiologic diagnosis of AD were included. The analysis included data for up to 5 UDS visits. Participant characteristics included age, sex, race, ethnicity, years of education, marital status, and living alone status. Dementia severity was measured by the global CDR. dataset_context_from_paper: An international, longitudinal cohort launched in 2010 to accelerate biomarker discovery in Parkinson's disease. The authors utilized longitudinal phenotype and whole-blood DNA methylation data from the PPMI cohort to calculate seven epigenetic aging measures (Horvath v1, Hannum, PhenoAge, GrimAge v1/v2, AltumAge, DunedinPACE) and assess motor function using the MDS-UPDRS.

dataset_context_from_paper: Longitudinal AD-related cohort used to examine the association between age at biomarker-clock events and remaining time to clinical symptom onset. Authors analyzed five biomarkers in this cohort: (1) CSF Abeta42/Abeta40, (2) CSF p-tau181, (3) plasma p-tau181, (4) amyloid PET, and (5) plasma p-tau217. The standard analysis produced uniformly significant associations for ages at biomarker-clock events based on all five biomarkers (hazard ratios 1.94-3.34, all P < 0.01). Time-varying analysis showed that younger age at biomarker-clock events is associated with higher hazard for symptom onset on the age scale.

dataset_context_from_paper: Retrospective longitudinal data from the Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative was used to train supervised logistic regression models to estimate the probability of undergoing DBS during follow-up. Separate models were developed for bradykinesia/rigidity–predominant, tremor‐predominant phenotypes, and the total cohort. Analyses were restricted to visits within a clinically plausible DBS screening window (age <75 years, Hoehn & Yahr stage 2–3, MoCA ≥26). Across 1,227 patients, phenotype‐specific and combined models demonstrated moderate discrimination for eventual DBS implantation (AUC 0.80–0.82).

The AMP-AD consortium provides harmonized multi-omics datasets generated from post-mortem brain tissue of individuals with Alzheimer's disease and age-matched cognitively normal controls, including RNA sequencing data from multiple brain regions and independent cohorts. Data were accessed through the AMP-AD Knowledge Portal, which supports standardized processing pipelines, metadata annotation, and cross-cohort analyses. For this study, AMP-AD datasets were queried to assess the expression patterns of the DEGs identified. AMP-AD is a large-scale integrative resource that provides multi-omic data, including transcriptomic, proteomic, and genomic profiles from multiple brain regions of well-characterized human cohorts. dataset_context_from_paper: The Bio-Hermes plasma proteomic dataset and associated phenotypic data are available through the AD Workbench platform of the Alzheimer's Disease Data Initiative under a controlled-access Data Use Agreement. Plasma proteomic measurements were collected from individuals with known amyloid status using tandem mass spectrometry with a TMTpro18 pipeline. The dataset included 992 participants after quality control and normalisation, with 881 proteins initially available. After complete-case analysis excluding features with missing values, the final dataset comprised 988 samples and 295 proteins. Five proteins showed significant differential expression after FDR correction, and 31 proteins with amyloid-status group differences were selected for machine learning training.

dataset_context_from_paper: The NACC database is funded by NIA/NIH Grant U24 AG072122. Following initial training on the UK Biobank dataset, an adaptive transfer learning approach was employed to calibrate estimates to the clinical dataset from NACC. 80% of NACC healthy controls (NC train, N=1,624) were used to recalibrate model parameters, establishing a NACC-specific normative baseline. The remaining 20% of healthy controls (NC test, N=394), along with all patients diagnosed with Alzheimer's Disease (AD, N=618), MCI Stable (N=632), and MCI Progressive (N=299), formed the test set for evaluating deviations from the normative model (total test set N=1,943). All sites included in the test set were also represented in the adaptation dataset to ensure proper calibration of site-specific parameters.

dataset_context_from_paper: Data presented in this manuscript are derived from the National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center (NACC) dataset, available upon request from https://naccdata.org/. The dataset includes cognitive assessment variables: CDR-SB (CDRSUM), Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE; NACCMMSE), logical memory immediate recall (LMI; LOGIMEM), logical memory delayed recall (LMD; MEMUNITS), time elapsed since LMI (MEMTIME), digit span forward (DSF; DIGIF), digit span forward length (DSFL; DIGIFLEN), digit span backward (DSB; DIGIB), digit span backward length (DSBL; DIGIBLEN), Trail Making Test Part A (TMT-A; TRAILA), Trail Making Test Part B (TMT-B; TRAILB), Wechsler Adult Intelligence Scale Digit Symbol Substitution Test (WAIS), animal fluency (ANIMALS), vegetable fluency (VEG), and Boston Naming Test 30 odd items (BNT; BOSTON). Data were downloaded with permission from NACC and sourced from 37 Alzheimer's Disease Research Centers (ADRCs) located across the United States. Standardized Uniform Data Set (UDS) version 3 variables, Neuropathology (NP) Data Set version 11 variables, and Genetic Data Set variables were used. Study analyzed trajectories of global cognitive assessments in subjects with various isolated neurodegenerative pathologies including Alzheimer's disease neuropathologic change, Lewy body dementia, and other pathologies.
